Your export app likely truncated the file during writing, leaving the IEND chunk incomplete or missing entirely. While some image viewers are lenient and can display the image data despite this structural flaw, Pillow’s newer versions enforce strict compliance with the PNG specification, rejecting files that lack a proper ending. Since the truncation occurred at the export stage, the file is fundamentally incomplete rather than just having a mismatched header. Re-exporting the images from the source application will ensure they are written with complete and valid chunk structures, which is more reliable than attempting to manually repair the binary data. Therefore, the correct approach is to re-export them.
